criteria.evidence: One Set globally bounds actual binding+scope residents to 32 entries and 8 MiB charged bytes. Valid reads return their unchanged frozen revision even when cache admission is skipped; the individually-over-budget branch is source-confirmed, while the existing 2 MiB document cap makes that branch unreachable with today's 8 MiB cache limit.

A single object epoch captured before awaits fences invalidation without retained key/flight registries; completion rejects stale age/epoch or older-than-resident revision/read start. publish/recover/initialize invalidate at entry and in finally, including rejected, lost-ack and committed no-put paths. Ten controlled race/idempotent scenarios pass, including a read starting during a held write. Original in-flight responses may return revision 1 but cannot repopulate after the tested invalidations. Retained W11 cases pass strict uncached authority, frozen values, read-start 30 s TTL, separate binding staleness, conditional conflicts/history/recovery/size and actual service failure behavior.

Both actual baseline-to-final deltas inspected; final fixture-only lifecycle.status as-const correction reverses exactly to the pre-read hash. limitations: Global 32-entry/8 MiB limits bound charged cache residency, not all JavaScript heap, binding object internals, concurrent outstanding read allocations, native CPU/latency or a supported customer corpus.

Expiry removal is opportunistic on reads; an idle isolate may retain expired but bounded entries. Hits do not extend freshness. One global epoch conservatively suppresses unrelated in-flight admissions while unrelated resident entries remain available.

Already-running calls may return their original validated revision; local invalidation fences cache refill, not cancellation. Distinct remote bindings/isolates retain the existing read-start 30 s staleness boundary.
